Keys are set in Options > Mods > Living World.

Hold Back, point at Living World and let go: the mod's wheel opens (management, cards, run with me, call the team here, zones, help). Point at a slice and press A, or hold Back, point and let go. In the mod's windows the D-pad moves, A picks, B closes, LB and RB change the tab or page, the right stick scrolls the text and Back gives the controls back to your character. Near someone, Interact (X) opens their menu. A zone is marked by walking: stand on a corner, press Y, walk to the other corner and close the zone on the wheel.
NPC creator button in the management window or the main menu
Narrator button in the Chronicle tab of the management window
in a passenger seat, right-click the ground
team button on the left sidebar
Help button in the Team window
The Zones window: pick the kind and drag on the ground; each zone is painted in its color.

Right-click the ground > Zones opens the window. Pick the kind, then click and drag on the ground: wood area, storage, foraging, farm, guard post, home (with the base's beds) and forbidden area, where the team does not go. Zones of the same kind cannot overlap: several side by side, like the rooms of one house, count as one. A zone covers only the floor it was marked on: in a house with an upstairs, mark each floor. <LINE> <LINE> The home marks the base: the jobs happen there, and those who work keep producing while you are away.
The Base window: needs and stock goals.

The Base window shows what the community needs: days of food, beds, safety (barricaded windows, zombies near) and morale. <LINE> <LINE> Stock goals say how much to keep: "20 planks" makes the team stop at 20 and start again when it drops.
The rules: what the team may take from storage on its own.

In the stock rules you choose which storages the team may take from, whether they may eat the last food and how much medicine to keep. Starving or parched, a person takes even reserved items and the last food, and tells you in the News. <LINE> <LINE> In a storage container's menu, "Container for" says what kind of thing it keeps. In a home door's menu, "Door" keeps it open, closed or automatic. In a bed's menu, "Bed of" gives it to someone of the team: that person sleeps there when at the base or near it, and the others leave it free.
Right-click the ground > Team orders > Build here.

"Build here" asks the team for a piece at that spot: wall, fence, gate, barricade, sandbags, rain barrel and other pieces from the base game. Each piece's tip says its cost, the skill and who on the team knows how. <LINE> <LINE> Whoever has the job "Build and repair" builds it with the storage's material and mends what is worn. The base must be marked. <LINE> <LINE> On the ground of a marked build, "Cancel the build here" undoes the request, and "Cancel all builds" clears the list.
Ana (red), Bruno (blue) and Carla (green) walk to the doors of the car you sat in.

Whoever follows you gets in your car: when you sit in a car that stands still, each one walks to a free door and takes a seat. Those told to "Stay here" do not come. Scared or hurt, they still run for the car, unless a zombie stands by the door, and they bandage their wounds once seated. <LINE> <LINE> You drive and they ride along. When you get out, they get out right after and follow you on foot. <LINE> <LINE> If the car moves before someone reaches a door, they are left behind.
Ana (red) took the wheel: right-click the ground to tell her where to go.

Sit in a passenger seat with the driver's seat free: the first one following you takes the wheel. <LINE> <LINE> Right-click the ground, or the world map, and pick "Drive here": they take the car along the streets, with the game's own gears, fuel and noise. <LINE> <LINE> Where they are going shows as a green square on the ground and on the map, with the way there along the streets. <LINE> <LINE> "Stop the car" (on the ground, the map or the car's menu) stops on the way. If you get out of the car, they stop too.
A team member at the wheel
A bandit gang arrives in a car painted in its color.

Cars belong to groups: bandit gangs drive cars painted in their color, and the bigger bases keep theirs. Someone driving on their own is rare. <LINE> <LINE> A gang in a car may stop near you, get out and come after you; then it goes back to the car and drives on. Away from you the trip goes on, and the car reaches their base and becomes the base's. <LINE> <LINE> At your base, the job "Repair cars" looks after the team's cars.
Ana's stance (red): aggressive, defensive or don't fight.

The stance says how willing the person is to fight: aggressive goes after zombies, defensive fights when needed, and "Don't fight" runs whenever it can. <LINE> <LINE> They fight on their own with the best weapon they carry, shove and stomp fallen zombies, back off when it is too much and help a teammate who went down.
When to shoot, and how many rounds to keep for danger.

Shots are loud and draw zombies. Here you decide when to shoot: by the stance, melee only, only in danger or freely. <LINE> <LINE> "Keep rounds for danger" has the person use a melee weapon while that reserve is all they have. They reload on their own with the ammo they carry.
The Gear tab: everyone's weapon, ammo, stance and firearms.

The Gear tab shows each one's weapon and ammo, and changes everyone's stance and firearms in one screen. <LINE> <LINE> Against people the fight is different: a gang may demand what you carry before attacking, surround you, run when losing and even surrender. See Dangers.
The NPC creator with a person made by the Random button.

The NPC creator designs people for the world: name, sex, skin, hair and its color, beard, clothes, weapon and the group they may turn up in (any, survivors, bandits, cult, military or police). The whole body shows on the right. <LINE> <LINE> "Random" rolls a new person (name, look, clothes and sometimes a weapon) without touching the group you chose, and "Save template" keeps it. Templates serve every save. <LINE> <LINE> Now and then a new person in the world is made from one of your templates, in the group you chose, one at a time. The chance is in the world options. The creator opens from the main menu (bottom corner) and from the "NPC creator" button of the management window.
An organized gang (a militia in camo) and, on the left, a cult in black robes.

Bandits live in their own bases and move in gangs, sometimes by car. A gang may demand what you carry before attacking: hand it over, negotiate a truce with their base, or fight. <LINE> <LINE> The losing side may flee or surrender; from the menu you spare or execute. They remember and may come back for revenge, or send a thief to your storage at night. Each gang has its color, and the most organized a uniform.
A cult: everyone in a black robe and its purple bandana.

Cults distrust strangers and hold rituals. An offering from the menu improves things. <LINE> <LINE> The military guard a perimeter around their base: whoever enters is warned and, if they stay, shot at. The police protect others from bandits and remember who kills innocents.
A bandit of a base demands something: their menu with Negotiate and Hand over.

When a bandit demands what you carry, their menu shows "Hand over" (pick an item of value) and, if they are from a base, "Negotiate": a truce with the whole base, or the ransom of someone they took, each with a price in items. <LINE> <LINE> In a deal you pay bit by bit and the menu shows how much is left. "Haggle" tries to lower the price once. The greedier they are, the likelier a no. <LINE> <LINE> Someone tied up by bandits shows "Untie" in their menu: freed, they thank you, go home on their own and remember you.
The narrator window: each with its own style, the chosen one highlighted.

A narrator decides when something comes your way: after a calm spell it brings a thief, a gang, someone passing by or someone from a community that knows you. It never makes people up: whoever comes already exists and had time to walk to you. <LINE> <LINE> The window opens when you start a new character and stays in Management > Chronicle > Narrator. The Watchman is steady. The Wanderer brings more passers-by and visits, and few attacks. Chance has no pattern. The Shadow draws more bandits as your team and food grow. A change applies at once. The pace and hostility of the world options still count. Now and then the narrator also speaks to you in a box at the top of the screen, never about what is coming. Options > Mods turns it off.
Bruno's card (blue), with a bleeding cut.

Survivors get scratches, cuts, bites, burns and fractures, bleed and fall ill. The card shows each wound. <LINE> <LINE> Rain soaks their clothes, cold brings hypothermia, a fall can break a leg and spoiled food poisons. They get tired and sleep on a free bed nearby, or on the floor. Someone following you sleeps only when you sleep or stay put for a while.
Bruno's menu (blue): bandage him with the bandage you carry.

They bandage themselves and stitch deep cuts when they have what it takes. Bleeding with no bandage, they tear a sheet or a piece of their clothes into strips (denim and leather only with scissors or a knife), and fetch a sheet or clothes from the storage when they have none. "Bandage wound" lets you do it for them with what you carry, "Change bandage" swaps a dirty one and "Examine wounds" lists each one. A sterilized bandage or disinfectant treats an infected wound. When they have time, they wash dirty bandages at a nearby sink, barrel or river. <LINE> <LINE> A bite brings the infection. A bitten person may hide it or tell; if they tell, you decide in the "The bite" menu: stay with the team to the end, wait away from it, leave, or end it before turning.
Giving an item to Dora (yellow): each item shows with its icon.

"Give item" hands over something from your inventory. Survivors carry real items, with weight, like you. <LINE> <LINE> They eat and drink on their own when needed, starting with what spoils first, open cans with a can opener or a knife (fetching one from the house) and cook raw meat on the stove. With the power gone, whoever has a lighter or matches lights a campfire with wood from the house. With nothing on them, they search containers and water sources nearby and ask you when they find none.
Ana's inventory (red), and what you can do with the bat she holds.

"Inventory" shows what the person carries. On each item: take, equip or unequip, wear or take off, eat, drink, open or drop. Also each piece's versions, like the hood down or the right shoulder; a second shoulder pad or knee pad goes on the free side. On their own they put the hood up in the rain and open a jacket in the heat. <LINE> <LINE> Their keepsakes (the house key and a memento) they never drop or trade; taking them away hurts. <LINE> <LINE> With someone of your team close by, they also show in the game's loot window, next to the containers. Drag items to give or take; right click one of their items to see what they can do with it.
Ana's job menu (red): each job with her priority.

"Job" gives the person jobs, each with a priority from 1 (first) to 4 (last). They do the most urgent one that has something to do. With little food or safety, those come first. <LINE> <LINE> There are jobs for wood, planks, foraging, farming, cooking, guarding, barricades, storage, corpses, the generator, animals, fishing, traps, hunting, cars, clothes and building. Whoever has a job stays at the base.
The Jobs tab: click a cell to change the priority.

In the Jobs tab of the management window each column is a job: click to go through 1, 2, 3, 4 and off. The arrows in the header show more jobs. <LINE> <LINE> Jobs use the zones you mark and fetch tools and material from storage, and what they make goes to storage. Boxes of nails and packets of seeds are opened right there. When something is missing, the person says what (no axe, no material...).
The Kitchen window: the meals at the base, the dishes, who cooks and the ingredients.

With the Cook job, people keep meals ready for the base: stew and soup in a pot of water, stir fry in a pan and salad in a bowl, cooked on the stove when they need it, and sandwiches on bread slices, with 2 to 4 ingredients from storage. They make first the dish furthest from its target. Hungry people eat right there, and the rest stays for the others. <LINE> <LINE> In the Kitchen window (Base tab, "Kitchen...") choose how many meals of each dish stay ready (0: not made) and which ingredients go in them. A meal cheers people up more than plain food, and a fine one (Cooking 4, 3 kinds of ingredient) even more.
Options > Mods > Living World: the keys and what shows on screen.

Options > Mods holds the keys (open the management window, "run with me"), the button on the left sidebar and what shows on screen: the affinity numbers, the mood faces, the people's voices, whether they use flashlights and the narrator's lines. <LINE> <LINE> The world options (sandbox, when you start a game) hold the rest: how many communities, bandit bases, cults, police stations and military bases at the start, newcomers, the pace of encounters and hostility, calm days at the start, radio, cars, betrayal, friendly fire between people and between you and your team, how well people aim and how much they take, the bite chance, the chance of your templates, and companions at the start.
The menu of Ana (red), who is on your team.

"Come with me": the person follows you, opens doors, climbs through windows and over fences, uses stairs and runs along. <LINE> <LINE> "Stay here": they wait and defend that spot. Whoever has a job stays at the base. <LINE> <LINE> When scared, they may refuse an order that leads near many zombies, and say so. If they distrust you, they do not obey. "Let go from the team" lets the person go their own way.
Come with me and Stay here

"Loot this building" sends someone for one kind of thing (food, medicine, weapons, tools, materials, clothes or everything) in a building the team has seen inside. What they find goes to the base storage. <LINE> <LINE> With two "patrol points" or more, "Start patrol" has someone walk between them on watch. <LINE> <LINE> "Build here" is in the Building topic. "Cancel the order" stops an order given. <LINE> <LINE> "Clear the patrol points" starts the route over.
Right-click the ground: call the team (Ana, Bruno and Carla) to a spot, or run with everyone.

"Call the team here" sends everyone to that spot. <LINE> <LINE> "Team: run with me!" makes everyone stop fighting and run after you, even those out of your sight. You can set a key for it in Options > Mods.
The game's gesture wheel (hold Q), Group: Ana (red) sees you.

The game's gestures (hold Q) speak to the people who see you. "Follow Me"/"Follow Behind": your team follows you; "Stop"/"Freeze": they stay; "Come Here"/"Come": they come to you and wait. They may refuse, as from the menu. <LINE> <LINE> "Wave Hi": the person in front of you greets you and waves back. "Thumbs Up", "Thank You", "Clap": they like you a little more; "Insult", "Thumbs Down": a little less (only a little each day). <LINE> <LINE> Bandits only scoff at "Surrender" and "Cease Fire". Turn it off in Options > Mods.
Right-click the ground > Team radio, with a walkie-talkie on.

With a walkie-talkie on, and another one with the person, you talk to a team member far away: "Where are you?", "Come to me" or "Meet me here". They answer on the radio and warn you when they see danger or run out of food or water.
The communities' radio, kept in the News.
Communities talk on a radio frequency: who is on the air, who is gone, whom to fear. A radio tuned to it plays the lines, and what you heard stays in the News.
Dora (yellow) says no: she lives in a community and will not leave her people.

"Invite to the team" asks if the person wants to come with you. They decide by what they think of you and by how they are doing: alone, hungry or thirsty, hurt or homeless makes it easier. Living in a community, being loyal to it or leading it makes it harder. <LINE> <LINE> Someone who distrusts you will not even think about it. A refusal lasts 12 hours: try later, or earn their trust first. <LINE> <LINE> Whoever joins leaves their old community and follows your orders.
Trading with Dora (yellow): on the left what you give, on the right what she gives.

"Trade" opens the trade window. Pick with the arrows what you give and what you want. The bar in the middle says whether they accept. <LINE> <LINE> Each person values things their own way: medicine, food and weapons are worth more, and what their community lacks is worth double. The more they like you, the less they ask over the value. <LINE> <LINE> A fair trade raises trust.
Your team, Ana (red), Bruno (blue) and Carla (green), and Dora (yellow), whom you do not know yet.

The world has other survivors. Each one is hungry, thirsty, tired and afraid, has memories and a life from before. They look for food, run from zombies and live in shelters with their community, even far from you. <LINE> <LINE> They say short lines over their heads to show what they feel and why they act: hungry, scared, stuck, no work... <LINE> <LINE> Right-click a person to open their menu. The next pages explain it.
Dora's menu (yellow): the first line says what she thinks of you.

The menu carries the person's name. Its first line shows their attitude toward you and their group: green is ally or friendly, white is neutral, red is wary or hostile. <LINE> <LINE> With someone outside your team you can invite them to the team, trade, ask about their life before, give an item or bandage them. Someone who distrusts you refuses almost everything. <LINE> <LINE> "Group colors" shows the color their community or gang wears: a scarf, a bandana, sometimes the whole outfit.
After a gift, Dora's attitude (yellow) goes up: the number shows over her head.

Attitude comes from what the person remembers of you and what they heard. Helping, giving gifts, fair trades, bandaging and saving someone raise trust. Stealing from their home, attacking and leaving someone behind lower it. Communities talk: what you do in one reaches the others. <LINE> <LINE> When the attitude changes, a number shows over the person's head. <LINE> <LINE> Taking something from a resident's home without asking, in front of them, is theft. Ask first, from the menu: "Ask to take things from the house".
The cards of Ana (red), Bruno (blue) and Carla (green).

The Team window ("Cards" in the management window, or "Team" in someone's menu) has a card for each member: what they are doing and why, their mood, health, hunger, thirst and fear, their traits, weapon, old job and wounds. <LINE> <LINE> Each card's button gives the order "Come with me" or "Stay here". "Manage" opens the management window.
The overview: everyone in one table, and on the right who needs attention.

The management window (the team button on the left sidebar, or the key in Commands and keys) puts everyone in a table, in tabs: Overview, Jobs, Gear, Base and Chronicle. The buttons on top open the News, the Cards (each one's full sheet) and the NPC creator, where you design people who may turn up in the world. <LINE> <LINE> Tick people in the first column and use the buttons below to give them all the same order: come with me, wait here, back to work or run with me. <LINE> <LINE> On the right you see who needs attention (hurt, hungry, unhappy...), and "Show me" takes you to the right tab.
The chronicle: what happened to the team, with an icon for each kind.

The Chronicle tab keeps what happened to the team: who joined and left, who was bitten, who died and of what, whom you helped or saved. The newest is on top. <LINE> <LINE> People remember each other too: friendships and quarrels on the team change everyone's mood.
The faces over their heads show how each one feels: Ana (red), Bruno (blue) and Carla (green).

Each one has a mood: it goes up with food, rest, talk and wins, and down with hunger, fear, wounds and deaths. Now and then a face rises over a head to show how they feel. You can turn it off in Options > Mods. <LINE> <LINE> They make bonds: those who talk and fight together become friends, and quarrels turn into grudges. The cards and the management window show who is unhappy with you. <LINE> <LINE> Someone who cares little for you and is greedy may betray you: they wait for you to sleep or look away, take the best of the storage and run. Good treatment and a friend on the team keep them. In the world options betrayal can be made rarer or turned off.
With the game sped up, Ana (red), Bruno (blue) and Carla (green) keep a few steps away.

Time speeds up with the mod's people around, and they go on with what they were doing. If someone still holds it at normal speed, a note says who: step away and click again. Walking, clicking another speed or a real zombie close undoes it. A fight nearby brings time back to normal until it ends. You can sleep with the team around: only a real zombie close stops you. <LINE> <LINE> Away from you the world goes on: the base produces, communities grow and trips go on. Sped up, even an expedition that sets out from near you goes on out of sight. Jobs make as much per game hour as at normal speed: the person stays put and does the steps without walking (all but hunting and the watch).
The base of Dora's community (yellow): log wall, barricades and the yard.

Other survivors live in communities, with a shelter, a leader and a color. Their base grows over time: barricades, a garden, a wall, a tower, a generator, until it becomes a stronghold. The kind of building and the residents' old jobs shape the base. <LINE> <LINE> They send expeditions, visit their neighbors, talk on the radio and sometimes fight each other. <LINE> <LINE> People outside your team keep out of your base on their own (your zones and the building where you sleep): they may come to talk or trade, but they do not take your things or move in.
The menu of Dora, a resident: her base's services, with the price.

A resident may offer services paid with items: treat your wounds in the infirmary, mend your weapon and clothes in the workshop, or stay the night. The price drops the more they like you. <LINE> <LINE> At a shelter's stall, a counter near the door, whoever stands behind it trades with the community's stock. Ask before taking things from someone's home.
The News: the help requests you heard.

When a community runs short of food, water or medicine, or someone is surrounded or taken by bandits, a resident asks you for help. The request stays in the News, a button of the management window. <LINE> <LINE> Giving what is missing, trading or bandaging answers it, and the community remembers. <LINE> <LINE> Someone taken by bandits is tied up at their base: see Dangers, "Negotiating and rescuing".
Opens the Jobs tab: give the Cook job there.
How many meals of this dish the kitchen keeps ready. At 0 it is not made.
Ingredients that may go in the dishes
Ticked: it may go in the dishes. Unticked: it stays out of them, to be eaten as it is.
No ingredients for the dishes in storage.
Every dish is at its target. The kitchen makes more once some are eaten.
Nobody has the Cook job. Choose who cooks.
Every dish is at 0: nothing to make.
Not enough ingredients for the missing dishes: each takes at least 2.
Nothing to make the missing dishes in: an empty pot, pan or bowl, or bread slices in storage.
No working stove at the base.
No tap or barrel with clean water near the storage.
A cook starts a dish when they have a moment.
Residents: %1. Suggested: about %2 meals in all.

Zones (base, storage, farm, forbidden):
right-click the ground > Zones.
Only what is near you is counted.
Nothing yet. What happens to the team is written here.
What happened to the team (page %1 of %2)
Nobody on your team yet. Right-click a survivor and choose "Invite to the team".
Key "%1": open or close. Tick people to give them orders. Cards: each one's full sheet.
Controller: Back > Living World opens this window. Tick people to give them orders. Cards: each one's full sheet.
More jobs: turns the page of job columns
Click a job: 1 (first) > 2 > 3 > 4 (last) > - (off). Whoever has a job stays at the base to work.
Nothing to clean the hutch with
%1 ran off with the pot. Didn't see it coming? Neither did I.
%1 was bitten. The dice don't care whose hand they're in.
Chance takes a seat at the table. Let's shake things up.
You picked me? Brave. Or bored.
Cold. Stamp your feet, it gets the blood going.
You made it to morning. Lucky.
New day, new hand. Let's see the cards.
A hundred days. Someone up there likes you. Not me, I'm just Chance.
A month. The odds are starting to give you funny looks.
Seven days. I wouldn't have bet on you. Good thing I didn't.
%1 is gone. Bad roll. No rematch.
Night is falling. At night the house always wins.
The sun is going down. Place your bets.
Heat like this, even the flies take a day off.
Call me Chance. I don't make plans and I don't keep promises.
Some days nothing happens. Some days everything does. I don't pick which.
Shuffle the cards, roll the dice. Let's see your luck.
%1 joined the game. More players, bigger pot.
Heads or tails? Doesn't matter. Pick one.
Today's lucky number is seven. Or three. Hard to say.
Somewhere a coin is spinning. Sooner or later it lands.
Don't look for a pattern. There isn't one. I checked.
Funny thing about luck: it never says when it runs out.
Today could be the most boring day of your life. Enjoy it.
First night. Beginner's luck lasts about this long.
Rain. Some call it bad luck. I call it Tuesday.
Wet socks. Luck smiles on nobody today.
Snow. Every flake different, like every one of my days.
Lightning never strikes the same place twice. Or so they say.
Oh, it's you. Let's see what the dice say today.
%1 ran off with your things. Everyone has a price.
%1 was bitten. You know how this ends.
The Shadow is here now. Let's count your things.
You called me. Few people do that on purpose.
Cold. A fire draws eyes. Remember that.
Daylight. You think the light protects you.
A hundred days. You built something. What is built can fall.
A month. People talk about you now.
A week. You're starting to have things worth taking.
The dark is coming. It always does.
Fog. Now you know how I see the world.
Heat makes people restless. And careless.
I am the Shadow. I notice what you have.
Have little, and I look away. Have much, and others look too.
Build what you want. Just remember who's watching.
%1 is with you now. One more mouth, one more name to remember.
%1 left. Less to feed. Less to lose.
The more you have, the more you have to lose.
Every full pantry tells a story to whoever finds it.
Someone always remembers where the food is.
Nothing you own is really yours. You're only holding it.
Your first night. The dark has many eyes.
Rain washes the blood away. Not the memory.
In the rain, everyone looks the same.
Snow. White, quiet, and it shows every footprint.
A storm. Good weather for things that don't want to be heard.
You came back. Everything is where you left it. For now.
Here again. Did you think I'd forget you?
%1 took what they could and vanished. Trust is hard to find now.
%1 was bitten. Spend the time that's left together.
The Wanderer here. Let's see who's still on the road.
My turn again. I missed the company.
Cold out. Somebody is burning their furniture tonight.
Another morning. Somewhere, someone else woke up thinking about food too.
Dawn. A good hour to leave, if you're leaving.
A hundred days. People will start telling stories about you.
A month. This land knows you by now.
One week. You've earned a little rest.
%1 died. I'm sorry. Some roads end too soon.
Evening. All over the county, people are lighting what they can.
The day is ending. I hope it treated you kindly.
In fog like this, a stranger is just a shape until they speak.
Hot one. The road shimmers and nobody walks far.
I'm the Wanderer. I've walked these roads longer than I'd like.
There are more people out there than you think. Not all of them want trouble.
Keep your door shut and your mind open. Let's see who you meet.
%1 joined you. A road is shorter with company.
%1 left. Maybe your roads will cross again.
Not everyone you meet is an enemy. Not everyone is a friend.
I once met a man who traded a radio for one quiet night of sleep.
Someone out there is keeping a diary. I hope they don't stop.
Every road leads somewhere. Most of them lead to a gas station.
People share more when they aren't afraid. Remember that.
A quiet road is a good road.
First night. You'll remember it, whatever happens.
Rain. Somewhere, someone is putting out every pot they own.

In percent: of what the NPC bases build (walls, towers, gardens, beds), how much comes from the map around them. The rest comes from runs out of sight.
